page: Amazon Web Services m8id.metal-48xl is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 96 physical cores and 192 vCPUs with a dedicated allocation running at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The CPU configuration includes a massive 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix and vector operations. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per physical core.

For local storage, the instance includes 11,400 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes, offering high-capacity, low-latency local storage. Networking capabilities feature a baseline bandwidth of 75 Gbps. In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, scoring in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core, PassMark CPU, and Geekbench multi-core tests. Memory performance is also highly competitive, with read-only memory bandwidth reaching top-tier status for both cached small blocks and uncached large blocks.

The hardware profile is highly optimized for data-intensive and parallel processing workloads. Benchmark data shows top-tier performance in database operations, Redis SET operations, static web serving throughput, and software compilation. Additionally, the presence of Intel AMX instructions enables strong performance in CPU-based LLM inference, particularly for prompt processing across small, medium, and large models. However, single-core performance remains in the average tier, indicating that workloads relying heavily on single-threaded execution may not fully leverage the massive scale of this bare-metal instance. It is best suited for large-scale databases, high-throughput web serving, containerized microservices, and parallelized data processing pipelines.
